questions.question: Find the value of the following expression: \(\frac{{3 \div 1 \times 2 + 5 - 2}}{{3 \times 3 - 2}}\)
questions.questionHtml:
Find the value of the following expression:

\(\frac{{3 \div 1 \times 2 + 5 - 2}}{{3 \times 3 - 2}}\)
questions.solution:
Concept used:

We would use the concept of BODMAS-

B – Bracket

O – Off

D – Divide

M – Multiplication

A – Addition

S – Subtraction

Calculation:

\((3\div1)\times 2+5-2\over (3\times 3)-2\)

⇒\(3\times 2+5-2\over 9-2\)

⇒ \(6+5-2\over 7\)

⇒ \(9\over 7\)

 ∴ The answer to the expression is \(9\over 7\).

questions.question: If \(P+\frac{1}{P}=5\) , then what is the value of \(P^3+\frac{1}{P^3}\) ?
questions.questionHtml: If \(P+\frac{1}{P}=5\), then what is the value of \(P^3+\frac{1}{P^3}\)?
questions.solution:
Given

P + 1/P = 5

Concept:

Cubic equation formula from quadratic equation: If P + 1/P = n, then P³ + 1/P³ = n³ - 3n

Solution:

P³ + 1/P³ = 5³ - 3×5

P³ + 1/P³ = 125 - 15 = 110

The value of P³ + 1/P³ is 110.

questions.question: \(\text{Simplify: } \left[ \left( \frac{1}{6} \div \frac{1}{9} \times \frac{2}{3} \right) \times 18 + 5 \right]\)
questions.solution:
Given:

E×pression: \(\left[ \left( \frac{1}{6} \div \frac{1}{9} × \frac{2}{3} \right) × 18 + 5 \right]\)

Formula used:

\(\frac{a}{b} \div \frac{c}{d} = \frac{a}{b} × \frac{d}{c}\)

For simplifying the entire e×pression, follow BODMAS (Brackets, Orders, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction).

Calculations:

Step 1: Simplify \(\frac{1}{6} \div \frac{1}{9}\):

\(\frac{1}{6} \div \frac{1}{9} = \frac{1}{6} × \frac{9}{1} = \frac{9}{6} = \frac{3}{2}\)

Step 2: Multiply the result by \(\frac{2}{3}\):

\(\frac{3}{2} × \frac{2}{3} = \frac{6}{6} = 1\)

Step 3: Multiply by 18:

1 × 18 = 18

Step 4: Add 5:

18 + 5 = 23

The value of the e×pression is 23.

questions.question: Which of the following statement is true? I. \(\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{6}+\frac{1}{12}=\frac{3}{4}\) II. \(\frac{1}{6}+\frac{1}{12}+\frac{1}{20}=\frac{3}{5}\)
questions.questionHtml:
Which of the following statement is true?

I. \(\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{6}+\frac{1}{12}=\frac{3}{4}\)

II. \(\frac{1}{6}+\frac{1}{12}+\frac{1}{20}=\frac{3}{5}\)
questions.solution:
Calculation:

Statement I:

⇒ \(\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{6}+\frac{1}{12}=\frac{3}{4}\)

⇒ \(\frac{6 + 2+1}{12}=\frac{3}{4}\)

⇒ \(\frac{9}{12}=\frac{3}{4}\)

⇒ \(\frac{3}{4}=\frac{3}{4}\)

LHS = RHS

Statement I is correct.

Statement II:

⇒ \(\frac{10 + 5+3}{60}=\frac{3}{5}\)

⇒ \(\frac{18}{60}=\frac{3}{5}\)

⇒ \(\frac{3}{10}=\frac{3}{5}\)

LHS ≠ RHS

Statement II is wrong.

∴ Option 1 is the correct answer.

questions.question: Find the greatest among the following options.
questions.questionHtml: Find the greatest among the following options.
questions.solution:

Concept Used:

Decimal conversion and comparison.

Calculation:

⇒  \(\frac{2}{3}\) could be written as 0.67 in decimal form

and,

questions.question: Which of the following statement is true? I. \(\frac{5}{11}>\frac{5}{6}\) II. \(\frac{5}{9}>\frac{8}{9}\) III. \(\frac{5}{6}>\frac{4}{5}\)
questions.questionHtml:
Which of the following statement is true?

I. \(\frac{5}{11}>\frac{5}{6}\)

II. \(\frac{5}{9}>\frac{8}{9}\)

III. \(\frac{5}{6}>\frac{4}{5}\)
questions.solution:
Given:

I. 5/11 > 5/6

II. 5/9 > 8/9

III. 5/6 > 4/5

Concept:

Fractions with the same numerator are compared based on their denominators. The fraction with the smaller denominator is greater.

Fractions with the same denominator are compared based on their numerators. The fraction with the larger numerator is greater.

Calculation:

I. 5/11 < 5/6 (5/11 is smaller than 5/6 as their numerators are equal and 11 is greater than 6)

II. 5/9 < 8/9 (5/9 is smaller than 8/9 as their denominators are equal and 5 is less than 8)

III. 5/6 > 4/5 (5/6 is greater than 4/5 as 55 > 64)

Therefore, the only true statement is III. 5/6 > 4/5.

questions.question: Simplify the following expression. \(\frac{{\left( {777 \times 777 \times 777} \right) + \left( {423 \times 423 \times 423} \right)}}{{\left( {777 \times 777} \right) - \left( {777 \times 423} \right) + \left( {423 \times 423} \right)}} \times \frac{1}{{\left( {77 - 47} \right)}}\)
questions.solution:
Given:

\(\frac{{\left( {777 \times 777 \times 777} \right) + \left( {423 \times 423 \times 423} \right)}}{{\left( {777 \times 777} \right) - \left( {777 \times 423} \right) + \left( {423 \times 423} \right)}} \times \frac{1}{{\left( {77 - 47} \right)}}\)

Formula used:

\(x^3+y^3=(x+y)(x^2-xy+y^2)\)

Calculation:

Using \(x^3+y^3=(x+y)(x^2-xy+y^2)\), 

\(\frac{{\left( {777 \times 777 \times 777} \right) + \left( {423 \times 423 \times 423} \right)}}{{\left( {777 \times 777} \right) - \left( {777 \times 423} \right) + \left( {423 \times 423} \right)}} \times \frac{1}{{\left( {77 - 47} \right)}}=\frac{(777+423) \left( {\left( {777 \times 777} \right) - \left( {777 \times 423} \right) + \left( {423 \times 423} \right)}\right)}{{\left( {777 \times 777} \right) - \left( {777 \times 423} \right) + \left( {423 \times 423} \right)}} \times \frac{1}{{\left( {77 - 47} \right)}}=\frac{1200}{30}=40\)

∴ \(\frac{{\left( {777 \times 777 \times 777} \right) + \left( {423 \times 423 \times 423} \right)}}{{\left( {777 \times 777} \right) - \left( {777 \times 423} \right) + \left( {423 \times 423} \right)}} \times \frac{1}{{\left( {77 - 47} \right)}}\) =  40

questions.question: Simplify the following expression. \(\frac{3\frac{2}{3}-5\frac{7}{9}\div\frac{1}{3}\times1\frac{2}{13}}{\frac{2}{3}\ of\ 1\frac{1}{3}\div\frac{1}{3}}\)

Concept

BODMAS rule applies here.

First solve bracket values, after it solves the values related with 'Of', Then Divided value, afterward Multiply values, Then addition and subtractions values.

Calculation

\(\frac{3\frac{2}{3}-5\frac{7}{9}\div\frac{1}{3}×1\frac{2}{13}}{\frac{2}{3}\ of\ 1\frac{1}{3}\div\frac{1}{3}}\)

⇒ \([{11\over 3} - {52\over 9} × 3 × {15\over 13}]\over{2\over3} ×{4\over 3} ×3\)

⇒ \([{11\over3} -{20\over1}]\over {8\over9} × 3\)

⇒ \(11 - 60\over {3}\) × \(3\over 8\)

⇒  \(- 49\over 8\)

⇒ \(-6{1\over8}\)

∴ The value of \(\frac{3\frac{2}{3}-5\frac{7}{9}\div\frac{1}{3}\times1\frac{2}{13}}{\frac{2}{3}\ of\ 1\frac{1}{3}\div\frac{1}{3}}\) is \(-6{1\over8}\)
